findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether 'follows the word `is`/`remains`/`left`' means IMMEDIATELY precedes the sentinel (only optional whitespace between trigger word and sentinel token) or any earlier occurrence on the line; add an example covering the non-adjacent case (e.g., 'The value is currently TBD' → fires or passes?).
evidence: 'A sentinel fires only when it starts a line or bullet, follows `:` or `=`, or follows the word `is`, `remains`, or `left`'
ABSENCE: no adjacency qualifier ('immediately follows', 'directly precedes', 'with only whitespace between') is stated
Counter-example not covered by stated rule: 'The value is currently TBD' — 'is' precedes 'TBD' non-adjacently
findings.finding: The sentinel firing condition 'follows the word `is`, `remains`, or `left`' does not specify whether the sentinel must IMMEDIATELY follow (only whitespace between the trigger word and the sentinel token) or whether any occurrence of the trigger word earlier on the same line qualifies. This is a real implementation fork: 'The value is currently TBD' would fire under a non-immediate interpretation but arguably should not, while 'status is TBD' should fire under both. An implementer must choose without guidance.
findings.location: Approach — sentinel firing rule, second bullet
scenarios: 'The value is currently TBD' would fire under loose interpretation, producing a false positive
An implementer chooses strict adjacency; another chooses line-scope — tests written for one fail under the other
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'immediately precedes (separated only by whitespace)' to the firing rule, e.g.: 'follows the word `is`, `remains`, or `left` with no intervening tokens'. Add a negative control in the ACs: 'The value is currently TBD' (trigger word and sentinel separated by an intervening word) does not fire.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that single-word suppression terms (especially `no`) must match as complete words (word-boundary anchors, e.g. `\bno\b`), not substrings, to prevent false suppression on words like `annotation` or `unknown`.
evidence: Plan states: 'Suppress a sentinel match when its same line contains a removal or negation term from this exact case-insensitive list: `no`, `zero`, `remove`, ...'
No word-boundary qualifier is specified for single-word tokens in the suppression list.
A line such as `annotation: TBD` contains the substring `no` inside `annotation` and would suppress the match under a naive substring implementation.
findings.finding: The sentinel suppression term `no` is listed without a word-boundary constraint; a substring match would suppress valid sentinel hits inside words like `implementation`, `annotation`, or `unknown`, silently passing plans that should fail.
scenarios: A plan line `annotation: TBD` should fail the sentinel rule but passes if `no` is matched as a substring.
A line `unknown status: TODO` contains `no` inside `unknown` — same false suppression.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note to the Approach: 'Each single-word suppression term is matched as a complete word (word boundaries); substring occurrences inside other words do not suppress.'

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an Acceptance Criterion verifying that the legacy compatibility clarity score is unchanged for inputs that contain no empty-body checkboxes and no sentinel assignments (i.e., pre-existing behavior is preserved).
evidence: Context: 'without changing ticket-type exemptions or the legacy compatibility score'
Approach: 'preserving the existing clarity score as compatibility coverage'
ABSENCE: No AC reads 'The existing clarity score/compatibility score is unchanged' or equivalent
findings.finding: The Context/Problem and Approach both explicitly state that the legacy compatibility score must be preserved unchanged, but no Acceptance Criterion verifies this constraint. An implementer could inadvertently break the existing clarity score without any AC catching it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria section (all 11 items); Approach — 'preserving the existing clarity score as compatibility coverage'; Context — 'without changing...the legacy compatibility score'
scenarios: An implementation that accidentally changes the scoring formula or weight passes all 11 ACs but violates the stated constraint, shipping a regression in legacy compatibility behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: '- [ ] A plan that previously passed clarity (no empty checkboxes, no sentinel assignments) continues to produce an identical clarity score after this change.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out plan (e.g., a feature flag to disable the new floors, an expand-contract migration step, or a documented revert procedure) so that unintended gate breakage can be reversed without a full redeploy.
evidence: 'Standalone clarity and deterministic P1 must enforce the same floor' — confirms plans currently passing will now fail
'preserving the existing clarity score as compatibility coverage' — only partial mitigation; gate outcomes still change
No rollback path, feature flag, or expand-contract step is mentioned anywhere in the plan
T4 criterion explicitly states: 'The remedy is an explicit rollback/back-out plan or expand-contract — acknowledgement alone is insufficient'
findings.finding: The plan changes gate pass/fail behavior for previously-accepted plans (empty AC items and unresolved sentinels now fail standalone clarity and P1) — a behavioral breaking change — but provides no rollback/back-out path or expand-contract sequence if the new floors cause unintended breakage in existing pipelines.
findings.location: Approach section: 'Wire the shared result into standalone clarity_check_compute and plan-review p1_readiness_shape'
scenarios: A legitimate plan that happens to contain a sentinel token in a prose context not covered by the suppression list is now blocked by CI with no way to unblock short of a code rollback.
An existing integration that programmatically checks gate outcomes now sees new failures it wasn't designed to handle.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line flag (e.g., `REBAR_CLARITY_FLOOR=0` env var or a config key) that disables the new hard-floor checks, making the change opt-in for one release cycle before becoming the default. Document the flag and its planned removal date in the Scope section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that `_plan_clarity.py` has ≥3 real call-sites, OR justify its extraction at 2 call-sites by explaining what makes the shared boundary clearly worth the indirection (e.g., the logic is complex enough that duplication risk outweighs the Rule-of-Three threshold).
evidence: Plan Scope: 'Add `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py` for the shared structural parser and hard-floor result.'
Plan Approach: 'Wire the shared result into standalone `clarity_check_compute` and plan-review `p1_readiness_shape`' — these are the only two named consumers.
No third call-site is named or implied anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The proposed `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py` abstraction has only 2 named call-sites (gates.py and det_floor.py), below the Rule-of-Three threshold of ≥3 for justifying a new shared module.
findings.location: Scope section — `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py`; Approach section — 'Wire the shared result into standalone `clarity_check_compute` and plan-review `p1_readiness_shape`'
scenarios: With exactly 2 consumers, any future change to the shared API requires updating both sites anyway, providing no abstraction benefit over inlining the logic — the module becomes indirection without reuse.
If one consumer's requirements diverge (e.g., gates.py needs different suppression logic for ticket types), the shared module must grow conditional branches, increasing coupling.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before introducing `_plan_clarity.py`, evaluate whether the new body-join and sentinel-scan logic can be layered onto (or extracted from) the existing `ac_item_lines` function in `det_operator_attested.py`, which is already a production helper accessible to both `det_floor` and `gates.py`, rather than writing a fourth near-identical AC-section walker.
evidence: `_count_ac_reset` in `src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py` lines 49-61: iterates lines, resets on `## `, counts `- [` items under `## Acceptance Criteria`.

`_count_ac_items` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` lines 155-169: documented as 'Mirrors gates._count_ac_reset so the DET floor shares the exact vocabulary of the standalone check_ac gate.'

`ac_item_lines` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_operator_attested.py` lines 25-37: same `## Acceptance Criteria` section walk, returns `- [` lines, already imported and called by `p6_ac_quality` inside det_floor.py.
`test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` lines 4-6 explicitly documents the two `_clarity_score` copies and their lockstep relationship, confirming the duplication pattern is known and managed.

The new helper in `_plan_clarity.py` extends the existing walk with a body-join and sentinel scan — logic that could be layered onto `ac_item_lines` in det_operator_attested.py rather than written fresh.
findings.finding: The plan adds a fourth near-identical AC-section parser (`_plan_clarity.py`) when the codebase already contains three production variants (`_count_ac_reset` in gates.py, `_count_ac_items` in det_floor.py, and `ac_item_lines` in det_operator_attested.py), the last of which is already accessible from within det_floor and does the same line-by-line section walk.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Add one pure shared plan-structure helper. Inside the exact `## Acceptance Criteria` section, recognize standard `- [ ]` and `- [x]` checklist items'; Scope section — `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py`
scenarios: The next time the AC-section parsing boundary rule changes (e.g., supporting `###` nested headings), there will be four separate sites to update instead of one.
A reviewer comparing `_plan_clarity.py` to `ac_item_lines` will need to establish manually that they agree on section boundaries — a recurring audit burden.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines` (or factor a thin wrapper from it) to return `(checkbox_marker, joined_body)` tuples, then add the sentinel scanner as a separate pure function in the same module. Both `gates.py` and `det_floor.py` can import and call these without a new top-level module.

findings.finding: The sentinel-as-value pattern vocabulary — the specific token set (TBD, TODO, FIXME, ???) and the three structural 'value position' forms ((a) starts bullet/line, (b) follows ':' or '=', (c) follows 'is'/'remains'/'left') — is defined only in the referenced closed ticket e759-c562-e233-4108's comments, not reproduced anywhere in the plan. An implementer reading only the plan cannot determine which tokens and which syntactic positions constitute a firing match.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach or Scope section, add a 'Sentinel detection rule' block that lists: tokens = {TBD, TODO, FIXME, ???}; fires when the token (a) starts a list item or line, (b) follows `:` or `=`, or (c) follows `is`/`remains`/`left`; suppressed when the same line contains a negation/removal word (no, zero, remove, delete, reject, forbid, must not, without), or when inside a fenced/inline code span.

findings.finding: The suppression/negation word list that governs when a sentinel match is suppressed is not defined in the plan. AC4 states 'same-line removal or negation assertions do not trigger the sentinel rule' but never enumerates which words constitute a removal or negation assertion. The concrete list (no, zero, remove, delete, reject, forbid, must not, without) exists only in the closed ticket's comments.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach or Scope section: 'Suppression: a sentinel match on a line is suppressed when the same line contains any of: no, zero, remove, delete, reject, forbid, must not, without.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive rationale for the shared-module approach over the established lockstep-copy pattern (or adopt the lockstep-copy approach), and if the shared module is retained, explicitly state its import constraint (stdlib-only, no imports from `_engine_support` or `llm`) so the implementer knows the topology is safe.
evidence: det_floor.py line 204: '"""A copy of gates._clarity_score's heuristic ... Kept local so the DET floor never imports a CLI gate transitively, but intentionally identical in vocabulary."""'

The plan says 'Wire the shared result into standalone `clarity_check_compute` and plan-review `p1_readiness_shape`' without addressing whether the new shared module can be safely imported by both without transitively pulling in CLI-gate dependencies.
test_criteria_heading_collapse.py enforces lockstep by importing both copies and comparing them directly — a lockstep-copy approach the plan would be abandoning without explanation.
No positive rationale is stated for why the shared-module approach is better than the established lockstep-copy pattern.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a shared `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py` module to be imported by both `_engine_support/gates.py` and `llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`, but states no import-topology constraint for the new module; the existing codebase explicitly avoids this cross-package sharing (det_floor's `_clarity_score` is a deliberate local copy: 'kept local so the DET floor never imports a CLI gate transitively'), and no positive rationale is given for departing from that established lockstep-copy pattern.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Add one pure shared plan-structure helper'; Scope — 'Add `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py`'
scenarios: If `_plan_clarity.py` is placed in `src/rebar/` (not under `_engine_support/` or `llm/`) and imports only stdlib, it is topology-safe — but an implementer who imports anything from `_engine_support` or `llm` in it creates a cycle.
The existing module-size cap and import-cycle guard tests may fail if the shared module grows or its import graph is wrong.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either document the sentinel/suppression lists as intentionally stable constants (with a note that changes require a PR) in a brief ADR or AGENTS.md entry, OR expose them as module-level constants (not literals buried in logic) so they are trivially configurable; also add an ADR/design-note entry capturing the shared-helper architectural decision.
evidence: 'scan case-insensitively for the sentinel tokens TBD, TODO, FIXME, and ???' — exact hardcoded list

'Suppress a sentinel match when its same line contains a removal or negation term from this exact case-insensitive list: no, zero, remove, delete, reject, forbid, must not, without' — exact hardcoded list
No mention of configurability for either list
No ADR or AGENTS.md update mentioned despite introducing a new shared helper consumed across two gate surfaces
findings.finding: The sentinel token list (`TBD`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, `???`) and suppression term list (`no`, `zero`, `remove`, `delete`, `reject`, `forbid`, `must not`, `without`) are business-policy rules hardcoded in `_plan_clarity.py` with no mention of how they will be evolved or configured, and no ADR captures the new shared-module architectural decision.
findings.location: Approach section (sentinel and suppression term lists); Scope: `src/rebar/_plan_clarity.py`
scenarios: A future policy change needs to add `HACK` or `XXX` as sentinels — requires a code change rather than a config update.
A project-specific suppression term is needed — no extension point exists.
A new engineer encounters `_plan_clarity.py` consumed by both gate surfaces with no ADR explaining why a shared module was chosen over duplicating the logic.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_plan_clarity.py`, define `SENTINEL_TOKENS: frozenset[str]` and `SUPPRESSION_TERMS: frozenset[str]` as module-level constants with a docstring. Add two lines to AGENTS.md (or an `docs/adr/` entry) explaining the shared clarity floor and pointing to the module.
